content:
# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 8
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
35 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 2
**EMET (literal):** And-all the-men-of Israel assembled to the-king Solomon at-the-feast, in-the-month-of Ethanim — it is the-seventh month.

**LOGOS (formal):** And all the men of Israel assembled to King Solomon at the feast in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** All the men of Israel came together before King Solomon during the festival in the month of Ethanim, the seventh month.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** And-all the-elders-of Israel came, and-the-priests took-up ʾet-the-ark.

**LOGOS (formal):** And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When all the elders arrived, the priests took up the ark

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** And-they-brought-up ʾet-the-ark-of YHWH, and-ʾet-the-tent-of meeting, and-ʾet-all the-holy vessels that were in-the-tent. And-the-priests and-the-Levites brought-them-up.

**LOGOS (formal):** And they brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites brought them up.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** and brought it up, along with the tent of meeting and all its sacred furnishings. The priests and Levites carried them.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king Solomon and-all the-congregation-of Israel who-assembled to-him were with-him before the-ark, sacrificing sheep and-cattle that could-not be-numbered or-counted from-multitude.

**LOGOS (formal):** And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, who had assembled before him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** King Solomon and the entire congregation of Israel gathered before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that no one could keep count.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 7
**EMET (literal):** For the-cherubim spread wings to the-place-of the-ark, and-the-cherubim covered over the-ark and-over its-poles from-above.

**LOGOS (formal):** For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim overshadowed the ark and its poles from above.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The cherubim's wings spread over the place where the ark rested, sheltering the ark and its carrying poles from above.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 11
**EMET (literal):** And-the-priests could-not stand to-minister because-of the-cloud, for the-glory-of YHWH filled ʾet-the-house-of YHWH.

**LOGOS (formal):** so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The priests could not continue ministering because of the cloud — the glory of the LORD had filled the temple.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** Then Solomon said, "YHWH said he-would-dwell in-the-thick-darkness.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said he would live in a dark cloud.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 13
**EMET (literal):** I-have-surely-built a-house-of exaltation for-you, a-place for-your-dwelling forever."

**LOGOS (formal):** I have indeed built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell in forever."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** I have built a magnificent temple for you — a place for you to live forever."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 14
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king turned ʾet-his-face and-blessed ʾet-all the-assembly-of Israel, and-all the-assembly-of Israel was-standing.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then the king turned his face about and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The king turned to face the whole assembly of Israel, who were standing, and he blessed them.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** 'From the-day that I-brought-out ʾet-my-people ʾet-Israel from-Egypt, I-did-not choose a-city from-all the-tribes-of Israel to-build a-house for-my-name to-be there. But-I-chose David to-be over my-people Israel.'

**LOGOS (formal):** 'Since the day that I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, that my name might be there. But I chose David to be over my people Israel.'

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He said, 'From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I have never chosen a city in any tribe of Israel for a temple to be built for my name. But I chose David to rule my people Israel.'

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 17
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was with the-heart-of David my-father to-build a-house for-the-name-of YHWH, the-God-of Israel.

**LOGOS (formal):** Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** My father David set his heart on building a temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** And-YHWH said to David my-father, 'Because it-was with your-heart to-build a-house for-my-name, you-did-well that it-was with your-heart.

**LOGOS (formal):** But the LORD said to David my father, 'Whereas it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But the LORD told my father David, 'It is good that you wanted to build a temple for my name.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 19
**EMET (literal):** Only, you shall-not build the-house; but your-son who-comes-out from-your-loins — he will-build the-house for-my-name.'

**LOGOS (formal):** Nevertheless, you shall not build the house, but your son who shall come from your body, he shall build the house for my name.'

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But you are not the one who will build it. Your own son — he will build the temple for my name.'

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 24
**EMET (literal):** who kept for-your-servant David my-father ʾet-what you-spoke to-him. And-you-spoke with-your-mouth, and-with-your-hand you-fulfilled, as-this day.

**LOGOS (formal):** who have kept with your servant David my father what you declared to him. You spoke with your mouth, and with your hand have fulfilled it this day.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** You have kept the promise you made to your servant, my father David. With your own mouth you promised it, and with your own hand you have fulfilled it today.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 25
**EMET (literal):** And-now, YHWH, God-of Israel, keep for-your-servant David my-father ʾet-what you-spoke to-him, saying, 'There-shall-not be-cut-off for-you a-man from-before-me sitting on the-throne-of Israel — only if your-sons guard their-way, to-walk before-me as you-walked before-me.'

**LOGOS (formal):** Now therefore, O LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you promised him, saying, 'You shall not lack a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons pay close attention to their way, to walk before me as you have walked before me.'

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Now, LORD God of Israel, keep the other promise you made to my father David: 'You will always have a descendant sitting on the throne of Israel — if your sons are careful to walk before me as you have walked before me.'

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 26
**EMET (literal):** And-now, God-of Israel, let-your-word be-confirmed, please, that you-spoke to your-servant David my-father.

**LOGOS (formal):** Now therefore, O God of Israel, let your word be confirmed, which you spoke to your servant David my father.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** God of Israel, please confirm the word you spoke to your servant David.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 28
**EMET (literal):** And-turn to the-prayer-of your-servant and-to his-plea, YHWH my-God, to-hear the-cry and-the-prayer that your-servant prays before-you today —

**LOGOS (formal):** Yet have regard to the prayer of your servant and to his plea, O LORD my God, listening to the cry and to the prayer that your servant prays before you this day,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Yet, LORD my God, hear the prayer and the plea your servant is making before you today.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 31
**EMET (literal):** When a-man sins against his-neighbor, and-an-oath is-laid upon-him to-make-him-swear, and-he-comes and-swears before your-altar in-this house —

**LOGOS (formal):** If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath and comes and swears his oath before your altar in this house,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When someone wrongs another person and is required to take an oath, and they come and swear before your altar in this temple —

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 32
**EMET (literal):** then you, hear in-the-heavens, and-act, and-judge ʾet-your-servants, condemning the-guilty, to-bring his-way upon his-head, and-justifying the-righteous, to-give to-him according-to his-righteousness.

**LOGOS (formal):** then hear in heaven and act and judge your servants, condemning the guilty by bringing his conduct on his own head, and vindicating the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants: condemn the guilty and bring their actions down on their own heads, and vindicate the innocent by treating them as their innocence deserves.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 36
**EMET (literal):** then you, hear in-the-heavens, and-forgive the-sin-of your-servants and-your-people Israel — for you-teach-them the-good way in-which they-should-walk — and-give rain upon your-land that you-gave to-your-people as-an-inheritance.

**LOGOS (formal):** then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk, and grant rain upon your land that you have given to your people as an inheritance.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on the land you gave your people as their inheritance.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 37
**EMET (literal):** Famine when-it-is in-the-land, pestilence when-it-is, blight, mildew, locust, caterpillar when-it-is; when his-enemy besieges-him in-the-land-of his-gates — any plague, any sickness —

**LOGOS (formal):** If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence or blight or mildew or locust or caterpillar, if their enemy besieges them in the land at their gates, whatever plague, whatever sickness there is,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When famine or plague strikes the land, or blight or mildew, locusts or caterpillars — or when an enemy besieges any of their cities — whatever disaster or disease comes —

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 38
**EMET (literal):** any prayer, any plea that belongs-to any man, to-all your-people Israel, who knows each-one the-plague-of his-own-heart and-spreads-out his-palms toward this house —

**LOGOS (formal):** whatever prayer, whatever plea is made by any man or by all your people Israel, each knowing the affliction of his own heart and stretching out his hands toward this house,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** when any prayer or plea is made by anyone among your people Israel, each one aware of their own suffering and spreading their hands toward this temple —

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 39
**EMET (literal):** then you, hear in-the-heavens, the-place-of your-dwelling, and-forgive, and-act, and-give to-each-man according-to all his-ways, whose heart you-know — for you alone know ʾet-the-heart-of all the-sons-of men —

**LOGOS (formal):** then hear in heaven your dwelling place and forgive and act and render to each whose heart you know, according to all his ways — for you, you only, know the hearts of all the children of mankind —

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Forgive and respond. Deal with each person according to all their ways, since you know their heart — for you alone know every human heart —

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 41
**EMET (literal):** And-also to the-foreigner who is not from-your-people Israel, and-he-comes from-a-far land for-the-sake-of your-name —

**LOGOS (formal):** Likewise, when a foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, comes from a far country for your name's sake —

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** And when a foreigner — someone who is not one of your people Israel — comes from a distant land because of your reputation,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 42
**EMET (literal):** for they-will-hear ʾet-your-great name and-ʾet-your-strong hand and-your-outstretched arm — and-he-comes and-prays toward this house —

**LOGOS (formal):** for they shall hear of your great name and your mighty hand and of your outstretched arm — when he comes and prays toward this house,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** because they have heard about your great name, your mighty power, and your outstretched arm — when they come and pray facing this temple,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 43
**EMET (literal):** you, hear in-the-heavens, the-place-of your-dwelling, and-do according-to all that the-foreigner calls to-you, so-that all the-peoples-of the-earth may-know ʾet-your-name, to-fear you like your-people Israel, and-to-know that your-name is-called upon this house that I-have-built.

**LOGOS (formal):** hear in heaven your dwelling place and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to you, in order that all peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your people Israel, and that they may know that this house that I have built is called by your name.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you. Do this so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and reverence you, just as your people Israel do, and so they may know that this temple I have built bears your name.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 44
**EMET (literal):** When your-people go-out to-battle against their-enemy, in-the-way that you-send-them, and-they-pray to YHWH toward the-city that you-chose and-the-house that I-built for-your-name —

**LOGOS (formal):** If your people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatever way you shall send them, and they pray to the LORD toward the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When your people go to war against their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to the LORD facing the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your name —

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 46
**EMET (literal):** When they-sin against-you — for there-is-no man who does-not sin — and-you-are-angry with-them and-give-them before an-enemy, and-their-captors take-them-captive to the-land-of the-enemy, far or near,

**LOGOS (formal):** If they sin against you — for there is no man who does not sin — and you are angry with them and give them to an enemy, so that they are carried away captive to the land of the enemy, far off or near,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When they sin against you — and there is no one who does not sin — and you become angry with them and hand them over to their enemies, who carry them away as captives to their own land, whether far or near,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 47
**EMET (literal):** and-they-take-it-to-heart in-the-land where they-were-taken-captive, and-they-return and-plead-for-grace to-you in-the-land-of their-captors, saying, 'We-have-sinned and-acted-perversely; we-have-done-wickedly,'

**LOGOS (formal):** yet if they turn their heart in the land to which they have been carried captive, and repent and plead with you in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned and have acted perversely and wickedly,'

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** and when they come to their senses in the land of their exile and repent and plead with you, saying, 'We have sinned; we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly' —

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 50
**EMET (literal):** and-forgive your-people who sinned against-you, and-all their-transgressions that they-transgressed against-you, and-give-them compassion before their-captors, and-they-will-have-compassion on-them.

**LOGOS (formal):** and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all their transgressions that they have committed against you, and grant them compassion in the sight of those who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Forgive your people who have sinned against you. Forgive all their offenses against you. Cause their captors to show them mercy,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 58
**EMET (literal):** to-incline our-hearts to-him, to-walk in-all his-ways, and-to-keep his-commandments and-his-statutes and-his-judgments that he-commanded ʾet-our-fathers.

**LOGOS (formal):** that he may incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his rules, which he commanded our fathers.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** May he turn our hearts toward him, so that we walk in all his ways and keep the commands, laws, and rules he gave our ancestors.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 61
**EMET (literal):** And-let your-heart be complete with YHWH our-God, to-walk in-his-statutes and-to-keep his-commandments, as-this day."

**LOGOS (formal):** Let your heart therefore be wholly true to the LORD our God, walking in his statutes and keeping his commandments, as at this day."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** And may your hearts be fully committed to the LORD our God, living by his decrees and keeping his commands, as you are doing today."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 63
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon sacrificed ʾet-the-sacrifice-of the-peace-offerings that he-sacrificed to-YHWH: twenty-two thousand cattle and-a-hundred and-twenty thousand sheep. And-the-king and-all the-sons-of Israel dedicated ʾet-the-house-of YHWH.

**LOGOS (formal):** Solomon offered as peace offerings to the LORD twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people of Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon's fellowship offerings to the LORD totaled twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. In this way the king and all Israel dedicated the temple of the LORD.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 64
**EMET (literal):** On-that day the-king consecrated ʾet-the-middle-of the-court that was before the-house-of YHWH, for there he-made the-burnt-offerings and-the-grain-offerings and-the-fat-pieces-of the-peace-offerings, because the-bronze altar that was before YHWH was-too-small to-hold the-burnt-offerings and-the-gra...

**LOGOS (formal):** The same day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the grain offerings and the fat pieces of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that was before the LORD was too small to receive the burnt offerings ...

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** That same day the king consecrated the central part of the courtyard in front of the temple, because the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to hold all the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and the fat of the fellowship offerings. So he offered them there in the courtyard.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 65
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon held the-feast at-that time, and-all Israel with-him — a-great assembly, from-the-entrance-of Hamath to the-brook-of Egypt — before YHWH our-God, seven days and-seven days: fourteen days.

**LOGOS (formal):** So Solomon held the feast at that time, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt, before the LORD our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon and all Israel celebrated the festival at that time — a huge assembly of people from as far away as Lebo-hamath in the north to the Brook of Egypt in the south. They celebrated before the LORD our God for seven days, and then seven more days — fourteen days in all.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
